targets.title: Set Reconciliation with Nearly Optimal Communication Complexity
targets.authors: Yaron Minsky, Ari Trachtenberg, Richard Zippel
targets.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
targets.why_needed: Characteristic-polynomial set reconciliation: two peers exchange evaluations of a rational function whose roots are the set elements, recovering the symmetric difference in near-optimal bits but requiring the difference size to be known or bounded in advance. This is the predecessor line every range-based and rateless scheme in this domain compares against.

targets.title: Invertible Bloom Lookup Tables
targets.authors: Michael T. Goodrich, Michael Mitzenmacher
targets.venue: 49th Annual Allerton Conference on Communication, Control, and Computing
targets.why_needed: Introduces the Invertible Bloom Lookup Table (IBLT), a hash-table variant supporting a peeling decode that recovers listed keys from a fixed-size summary; the data structure every Difference-Digest-family set-reconciliation scheme in this domain builds on.

targets.title: What's the Difference? Efficient Set Reconciliation Without Prior Context
targets.authors: David Eppstein, Michael T. Goodrich, Frank Uyeda, George Varghese
targets.venue: ACM SIGCOMM
targets.why_needed: Difference Digests: an IBLT-based protocol that reconciles two sets in communication proportional to the symmetric-difference size without either side knowing that size beforehand, using invertible Bloom filters sized by an estimator. This is the deployed-scale foundation of the IBLT reconciliation family, and its per-hop bandwidth figures are the numbers a range-based scheme's claimed advantage must be checked against.

targets.title: Practical Rateless Set Reconciliation
targets.authors: Lei Yang, Yossi Gilad, Mohammad Alizadeh
targets.venue: ACM SIGCOMM
targets.why_needed: Rateless IBLT: an encoder that produces an unbounded stream of coded symbols from the set difference so the decoder stops as soon as it has received enough, removing the need to size the sketch in advance at all. States its own measured range of tested set-difference sizes and payload sizes; this is the foundational paper of the rateless-coded reconciliation family named in this domain's brief.

targets.title: CertainSync: Rateless Set Reconciliation with Certainty
targets.authors: Tomer Keniagin, Eitan Yaakobi, Ori Rottenstreich
targets.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Measurement and Analysis of Computing Systems (SIGMETRICS)
targets.why_needed: Addresses the failure condition rateless IBLT leaves open: decode can fail to terminate or return a wrong result with some probability. Extract what guarantee of successful termination this construction proves and at what overhead relative to Yang et al., since a synchronization primitive without a termination bound has an open failure mode the architecture must account for.

targets.title: Rateless Bloom Filters: Set Reconciliation for Divergent Replicas with Variable-Sized Elements
targets.authors: Pedro Silva Gomes, Carlos Baquero
targets.venue: arXiv preprint
targets.why_needed: Applies rateless coding to reconciliation of variable-length elements rather than fixed-length hashes, authored by one of the original CRDT co-authors (Baquero). Elements in a replicated log or CRDT operation history are variable-length, so this states whether rateless reconciliation composes with that data shape without a length-normalization step.

targets.title: Range-Based Set Reconciliation via Range-Summarizable Order-Statistics Stores
targets.authors: Elvio G. Amparore
targets.venue: arXiv preprint
targets.why_needed: Formalizes the storage-backend contract range-based set reconciliation (RBSR) needs (composable range summaries plus rank/select navigation), separates protocol complexity from storage complexity, augments B+-trees to realize it, and implements it as AELMDB integrated with Negentropy. Directly answers this domain's brief to find 2023-2026 work separating RBSR's protocol complexity from its local computational cost, and gives measured local-reconciliation-cost results on reconciliation-heavy workloads.

targets.title: Range-Based Set Reconciliation Without Homomorphic Hashing
targets.authors: Aljoscha Meyer, Konstantin Scherer
targets.venue: Technical report, Technische Universität Berlin (self-published, author's site)
targets.why_needed: Replaces range-based set reconciliation's requirement for a non-standard homomorphic hash function with an implementation over history-independent, clamping-invariant search trees usable with any conventional hash (e.g. SHA-family), removing a cryptographic-primitive dependency the 2023 SRDS paper had. Also directly compares against Merkle Search Trees (Auvolat and Taïani) on the same complexity criteria; extract that comparison's measured or derived basis rather than the paper's own 'renders MST reconciliation obsolete' claim, which is the authors' judgment, not a fact to carry forward per this pass's rule 2.

targets.title: Merkle Search Trees: Efficient State-Based CRDTs in Open Networks
targets.authors: Alex Auvolat, François Taïani
targets.venue: IEEE International Symposium on Reliable Distributed Systems (SRDS)
targets.why_needed: Merkle Search Tree (MST): a probabilistic balanced search tree whose node boundaries and structure are determined only by the content (history-independent), so that two replicas holding the same key set converge to an identical tree regardless of insertion order, letting the tree itself serve as a state-based CRDT and support Merkle-style content comparison for reconciliation. States the paper Meyer and Scherer (2024) directly compare against and claim to obsolete; both comparisons need this primary source's own numbers.

targets.title: Accelerating Prolly Trees: Simplified Chunking for Rapid Updates
targets.authors: Abhimanyu Rawat, Tarun Kumar Vangani, Hanno Cornelius, Vanesa Daza
targets.venue: Distributed Ledger Technologies Workshop (DLT), CEUR-WS
targets.why_needed: Prolly trees are content-defined-chunked B-trees where every node is content-addressed, giving Merkle-tree-style verification plus B-tree-style ordered range scans. States a deterministic chunking algorithm bounding a single insertion's restructuring to one chunk plus an O(height) anchor-path update, replacing the classical design's cascading rechunking, with measured hash-operation counts and insertion-time reductions on real workloads. Directly answers the brief's open question on 2023-2026 work on secondary indexes and range queries over content-addressed stores. An extended journal version appears in ACM Distributed Ledger Technologies: Research and Practice (DOI 10.1145/3785142).

targets.title: Cartesian Merkle Tree
targets.authors: Artem Chystiakov, Oleh Komendant, Kyrylo Riabov
targets.venue: arXiv preprint
targets.why_needed: Combines a binary search tree, a heap (treap structure), and a Merkle tree into one history-independent structure supporting O(log n) insertion, update, and removal plus membership and non-membership proofs. A treap-family alternative to Merkle Search Trees and to Meyer's zip-tree-based constructions for the same history-independence property RBSR over search trees requires; needed to compare tree-balancing mechanisms (randomized priority vs. content-derived split points) for the same convergence guarantee.

targets.title: Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types
targets.authors: Marc Shapiro, Nuno Preguiça, Carlos Baquero, Marek Zawirski
targets.venue: Stabilization, Safety, and Security of Distributed Systems (SSS)
targets.why_needed: States the two sufficient conditions for strong eventual consistency without coordination: state-based (CvRDT) replicas whose merge is a join on a semilattice, and operation-based (CmRDT) replicas whose concurrent operations commute, each proved sufficient in this paper. Every later CRDT paper in this domain is built on one of these two conditions, so a mechanism's classification as CvRDT or CmRDT determines what convergence proof it can reuse.

targets.title: Convergent and Commutative Replicated Data Types
targets.authors: Marc Shapiro, Nuno Preguiça, Carlos Baquero, Marek Zawirski
targets.venue: Bulletin of the European Association for Theoretical Computer Science (EATCS), No. 104
targets.why_needed: Expository classification of the CvRDT/CmRDT families with worked examples (counters, sets, sequences) at more length than the SSS conference paper; the open-access companion piece to cite for the taxonomy itself rather than for the formal proofs.

targets.title: Approaches to Conflict-free Replicated Data Types
targets.authors: Paulo Sérgio Almeida
targets.venue: ACM Computing Surveys
targets.why_needed: 2025 systematization of CRDT design approaches (operation-based, state-based, pure operation-based, delta-state) by one of the delta-state CRDT co-inventors. This is the domain's post-2023 survey and the source to check for which CRDT design questions the field considers open versus settled as of 2025, ahead of any per-mechanism selection.

targets.title: Replicated Data Types: Specification, Verification, Optimality
targets.authors: Sebastian Burckhardt, Alexey Gotsman, Hongseok Yang, Marek Zawirski
targets.venue: ACM SIGPLAN-SIGACT Symposium on Principles of Programming Languages (POPL)
targets.why_needed: Gives a formal, executable specification framework for replicated data types independent of any implementation, plus a proof technique for showing a given implementation meets a specification and a notion of optimality (no implementation can send less information and still meet the spec). Needed as the formal-methods yardstick for any measured-cost claim about a specific CRDT implementation in this domain.

targets.title: A Conflict-Free Replicated JSON Datatype
targets.authors: Martin Kleppmann, Alastair R. Beresford
targets.venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
targets.why_needed: The algorithm underlying Automerge: a CRDT for arbitrary nested JSON (maps, lists, and ordered text) built from a list CRDT with each list element addressed by a globally unique, causally-ordered identifier. States the paper's own memory and message-size measurements against Operational Transformation and other CRDTs, which is the primary source for any claim about Automerge's baseline cost before later encoding optimizations.

targets.title: OpSets: Sequential Specifications for Replicated Datatypes
targets.authors: Martin Kleppmann, Victor B. F. Gomes, Dominic P. Mulligan, Alastair R. Beresford
targets.venue: Archive of Formal Proofs
targets.why_needed: Machine-checked (Isabelle/HOL) formal framework proving that a family of list, map, and JSON CRDTs satisfy list/map sequential-specification semantics, independent of network delivery order. Needed as the machine-verified correctness backing for the JSON CRDT and text-editing CRDTs selected elsewhere in this domain; an extended version with the informal exposition is arXiv:1805.04263.

targets.title: Interleaving Anomalies in Collaborative Text Editors
targets.authors: Martin Kleppmann, Victor B. F. Gomes, Dominic P. Mulligan, Alastair R. Beresford
targets.venue: Workshop on Principles and Practice of Consistency for Distributed Data (PaPoC), co-located with EuroSys
targets.why_needed: States a correctness failure common to RGA-family sequence CRDTs (the family underlying much of Yjs and early Automerge): when two users concurrently insert text at the same position, some of these algorithms can interleave the two users' characters into a garbled result rather than keeping each contiguous. Extract the precise condition under which interleaving occurs and which named algorithms are and are not subject to it, since this bears directly on which sequence-CRDT variant is safe to select for collaborative text.

targets.title: Specification and Complexity of Collaborative Text Editing
targets.authors: Hagit Attiya, Sebastian Burckhardt, Alexey Gotsman, Adam Morrison, Hongseok Yang, Marek Zawirski
targets.venue: ACM Symposium on Principles of Distributed Computing (PODC)
targets.why_needed: Gives a formal correctness specification for collaborative text editing and proves a worst-case lower bound on the memory any correct algorithm must retain (a function of the number of concurrent edits), independent of which specific CRDT or OT algorithm is used. This is the primary source for a memory-cost floor to check any measured CRDT text-editing footprint in this domain against. An extended journal version with a tightened space bound is Theoretical Computer Science 855 (2021), DOI 10.1016/j.tcs.2020.11.046.

targets.title: A Highly-Available Move Operation for Replicated Trees
targets.authors: Martin Kleppmann, Dominic P. Mulligan, Victor B. F. Gomes, Alastair R. Beresford
targets.venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
targets.why_needed: A CRDT for a mutable tree (the data model of a filesystem directory hierarchy or a nested outline) supporting a move operation that concurrent operations from other replicas cannot turn into a cycle, without coordination. Needed wherever the application data model is a hierarchical structure rather than a flat map or sequence, which the flat JSON CRDT of Kleppmann and Beresford (2017) does not by itself resolve for move semantics.

targets.title: Yjs: A Framework for Near Real-Time P2P Shared Editing on Arbitrary Data Types
targets.authors: Petru Nicolaescu, Kevin Jahns, Michael Derntl, Ralf Klamma
targets.venue: International Conference on Web Engineering (ICWE)
targets.why_needed: The original paper describing Yjs's shared-editing framework and its internal replicated data-type representation, needed as the primary source for how Yjs's mechanism differs internally from Automerge's JSON CRDT even though both target the same class of collaborative-editing problem; a follow-up, 'Near Real-Time Peer-to-Peer Shared Editing on Extensible Data Types' (GROUP 2016), extends the same system.

targets.title: Making CRDTs Byzantine Fault Tolerant
targets.authors: Martin Kleppmann
targets.venue: Workshop on Principles and Practice of Consistency for Distributed Data (PaPoC), co-located with EuroSys
targets.why_needed: Extends the state-based and operation-based CRDT convergence proofs to a Byzantine setting, where some replicas may send different, contradictory operations to different recipients, using hash-chained operation logs so any two correct replicas that received the same log entries compute the same state even if a faulty replica tried to make them diverge. States the mechanism BeeKEM (already retrieved) explicitly builds on and cites as its CRDT foundation.

targets.title: Byzantine Eventual Consistency and the Fundamental Limits of Peer-to-Peer Databases
targets.authors: Martin Kleppmann, Heidi Howard
targets.venue: arXiv preprint
targets.why_needed: Defines Byzantine Eventual Consistency (BEC) as a correctness condition for peer-to-peer databases with malicious participants, and proves an impossibility result bounding what such a system can guarantee without a trusted party. Needed as the source for what causal-broadcast and CRDT convergence can and cannot promise once some peers are actively malicious rather than merely crash-faulty, ahead of the Byzantine-CRDT mechanism above.

targets.title: Concurrency Control in Groupware Systems
targets.authors: Clarence A. Ellis, Simon J. Gibbs
targets.venue: ACM SIGMOD
targets.why_needed: The original Operational Transformation (OT) paper: concurrent operations are transformed against each other so that, applied in a different order at each site, they still produce the same final document, requiring a central sequencer or agreed total order in the algorithms this paper presents. Needed as the OT baseline this domain's brief asks for, to compare against the CRDT family's ordering requirements.

targets.title: Operational Transformation in Real-Time Group Editors: Issues, Algorithms, and Achievements
targets.authors: Chengzheng Sun, Clarence A. Ellis
targets.venue: ACM Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work (CSCW)
targets.why_needed: States the transformation-property requirements (TP1, TP2) later OT algorithms must satisfy to remain correct under arbitrary concurrent-operation orderings, and surveys where early OT algorithms violated them. Needed as the source for OT's own stated correctness conditions and failure modes, for a fair comparison against CRDT convergence guarantees rather than an comparison against an unstated or idealized version of OT.

targets.title: High-Latency, Low-Bandwidth Windowing in the Jupiter Collaboration System
targets.authors: David A. Nichols, Pavel Curtis, Michael Dixon, John Lamping
targets.venue: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST)
targets.why_needed: The Jupiter protocol: a client-server OT scheme in which the server imposes total order and each client transforms its own pending operations against the server's acknowledged operation stream. This client-server OT design (later the basis of Google Wave's and Google Docs's OT implementations) is the direct point of comparison for why decentralized CRDT and Byzantine causal broadcast approaches in this domain avoid requiring a server to impose order.

targets.title: Local-First Software: You Own Your Data, in Spite of the Cloud
targets.authors: Martin Kleppmann, Adam Wiggins, Peter van Hardenberg, Mark McGranaghan
targets.venue: ACM SIGPLAN International Symposium on New Ideas, New Paradigms, and Reflections on Programming and Software (Onward!)
targets.why_needed: States seven requirements for local-first software (no spinners: work is fast; multi-device; offline-capable; supports real-time collaboration; the long now, meaning data readable indefinitely; privacy and security by default; user retains ultimate ownership and control) and argues CRDTs are the mechanism that satisfies several of them simultaneously. This is the requirements document the CRDT and synchronization mechanisms in this domain are being selected to satisfy, not itself a mechanism paper.

targets.title: ListGuard: Mitigating Pollution Attacks on In-Network Invertible Bloom Lookup Tables
targets.authors: Harish S A, Vignesh S, Sathwik Kodamarthi, Bikraj Shrestha, Gollapudi Sasank, Mahanth Kumar Valluri, Pravein G. Kannan, Praveen Tammana
targets.venue: IFIP Networking Conference
targets.why_needed: A pollution attack against in-network IBLT-based reconciliation: extract the injection mechanism that corrupts peeling decode and the measured decode-failure or false-recovery rate it causes, and the defense (ListGuard) proposed against it, since this bears directly on whether IBLT-based reconciliation is safe against an adversarial peer without added integrity checks.

targets.title: Breaking 2-Cores for Invertible Bloom Lookup Tables by Structure Prediction
targets.authors: Vojtech Gadurek, Pavel Veselý
targets.venue: Symposium on Experimental Algorithms (SEA), LIPIcs
targets.why_needed: Attacks the peeling-decode guarantee of IBLTs by predicting and exploiting 2-core structure (the substructure that makes standard peeling decode fail), open access via LIPIcs. Extract the measured decode-failure rate this construction forces at set sizes and load factors otherwise considered safe for IBLT decode, which bears on the safety margin any IBLT-based reconciliation parameter choice needs against an adversarial peer.

targets.title: Willow: 3d Range-Based Set Reconciliation (protocol specification)
targets.authors: Sam Gwilym, Aljoscha Meyer, and the Earthstar/Willow project contributors
targets.venue: willowprotocol.org, protocol specification (not a peer-reviewed paper), funded in part by NLnet
targets.why_needed: Generalizes range-based set reconciliation from a single ordered dimension to a 3-dimensional range (subspace, path, timestamp), so one reconciliation round can target the intersection of a namespace, a path prefix, and a time window instead of the whole ordered set. This is the deployed generalization named directly in this domain's brief; extract its concrete fingerprint-composition rule and how it partitions a 3dRange to recurse, since this is the working answer to whether range-based reconciliation extends to structured, multi-dimensional data rather than one flat ordered log.

targets.title: NIP-77: Negentropy Syncing (Nostr protocol extension for range-based set reconciliation)
targets.authors: Doug Hoyte (Negentropy protocol), wrapped for Nostr as NIP-77 by the nostr-protocol contributors
targets.venue: github.com/nostr-protocol/nips and github.com/hoytech/negentropy, protocol specification (not a peer-reviewed paper)
targets.why_needed: The deployed range-based-reconciliation implementation this domain's brief names directly, and the integration target of Amparore (2026)'s AELMDB storage backend. Its wire format fixes concrete parameters (fingerprint = SHA-256 of the modular sum of element IDs concatenated with the element count, truncated to 16 bytes; a Bound encodes a timestamp plus a variable-length disambiguating ID prefix) that give one real answer to how a homomorphic-style fingerprint is built from a conventional hash by using modular addition as the combining operation, relevant to Meyer and Scherer's homomorphic-hashing objection.
